note: Window agent m0700-m0601, 2 Nov 2026. Entries: keyframe_overrides/0 Wu core (Suzhou homonym); keyframe_overrides/1-2 Kush keyframes -700 and -675 cut to Nubia (Egypt is the Twenty-fifth Dynasty dossier's); keyframe_overrides/3 Assyria -675 without Egypt (the conquest began 671); keyframe_overrides/4-5 Lydia -650 and -630 years (the large shape from -620, as the dossier's text says).

correction.text: the Wuxi-Suzhou core of the early Wu in Jiangsu (Meili and Helu's City near Wuxi, then Gusu at Suzhou), -750..-585

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's spec {place: Suzhou, km: 60} resolves to Suzhou in Anhui (117.0E, 33.6N, 600 km from Wuxi), so the drafts draw a second Wu disc on the Huai. The page puts Wu's capitals in Jiangsu: first at Meili in Wuxi, then 'moved to Gusu (probably in modern Suzhou)'. The Suzhou disc is now fixed on Suzhou, Jiangsu (120.62E, 31.30N).

correction.text: Nubia alone (Cliopatria's Kush shape of -675: the Nile from the Butana to 23.8 N); Egypt in these years is the Twenty-fifth Dynasty's, drawn by that dossier

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's -700 Kush shape adds all Egypt to the Delta, which the twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt dossier already claims (keyframes -712..-672, the Nile Valley), so the compile gave the Nile ribbon to the dynasty and the Western and Eastern Deserts (about 1,500 cells) to Kush. The page: the dynasty 'originated in the Kingdom of Kush' and Shebitku 'conquered the entire Nile Valley, including Upper and Lower Egypt, around 712 BC'; Egypt is drawn once, as the dynasty.

correction.text: Nubia as drawn by Cliopatria at -675; Upper Egypt (Thebes), Kushite until 656, is the Twenty-fifth Dynasty's keyframes (-671 and -663 'Upper and Middle Egypt')

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's union with the region 'Upper Egypt' resolves to the whole governorates (New Valley and Red Sea included, 1,500 cells of desert), while the Nile cells go to the dynasty by the size rule: a ribbon inside a Kush donut. The page: Taharqa 'was defeated in Egypt in 671 BC when Esarhaddon conquered Northern Egypt' and Kushite control of Upper Egypt was lost 'in 656 BC when Psamtik I captured Thebes'; both are the dynasty dossier's keyframes.

correction.text: the empire without Egypt (Cliopatria's -675 shape is the post-conquest block) and without Urartu; Assyria took Memphis and the Delta only from 671 (the ledger's gains), valid -675..-656

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier cut only Upper Egypt, so the -675 snap handed Assyria the Sinai and a strip of the Matruh coast west of the Delta (about 190 cells) four years before the conquest. The page: 'Taharqa and his army defeated the Assyrians outright in 674', Esarhaddon 'raided Egypt in 673' and 'In 671, Esarhaddon took and sacked' Memphis; it names no Assyrian holding in Egypt or Sinai before 671. The -700 verdict already stops the empire at the Egyptian border.

correction.text: Unchanged shape (Troad, Hellespont coast, Caria), held to -621: Lydia's large shape begins in -620, when it 'expanded to incorporate much of Phrygia'

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own correction text says this shape is held to 621 instead of 631, but with no from/to the compile ends it at Cliopatria's -631. Years only; the shape is unchanged.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held from -620 (to -616) instead of -630: Lydia 'eventually expelled [the Cimmerians] by around 620 BC' and then 'expanded to incorporate much of Phrygia, which became the Lydian empire's eastern frontier'

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier says this shape holds from 620, but the compile starts it at Cliopatria's -630 and snaps 556 cells (Konya, Ankara, Eskisehir) ten years before the dated expansion; the ledger's own -620 gains (Phrygia, the peoples west of the Halys) now arrive first. The Lydia page gives no year for the eastward extension (only Alyattes' accession in 635).
